title: Regularity at bounded degree
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the sign cube $\\{−1,1\\}^n$, and let $\\varepsilon$ be real. Suppose every nonempty set of coordinates has Fourier coefficient of absolute value at most $\\varepsilon$. Then, for every nonnegative integer $k$, every nonempty set of at most $k$ coordinates has Fourier coefficient of absolute value at most $\\varepsilon$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a real-valued function on the sign cube
every nonempty coordinate set has Fourier coefficient of absolute value at most $\\varepsilon$
the coordinate set in the conclusion is nonempty and has size at most $k$
